LESSON: ULUM AL- HADITH

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Hadith
Topic 2.1: Ulum al- Hadith

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Ulum al- Hadith. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What role did the Prophet (S.A.W.) play in the development of Hadith?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs
2. explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith
3. apply the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith
4. value Hadith as a primary source of guidance
5. explain the relevance of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in the life of a Muslim
6. practise the teachings of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in daily life
7. appreciate Hadith as the second source of sharia

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ULUM AL- HADITH
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Ulum al- Hadith helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ULUM AL- HADITH
Study Ulum al- Hadith like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Ulum al- Hadith” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Ulum al- Hadith in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Value Hadith as a primary source of guidance

What this means
In this part you learn to value Hadith as a primary source of guidance. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value Hadith as a primary source of guidance.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Ulum al- Hadith” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value Hadith as a primary source of guidance. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Explain the relevance of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in the life of a Muslim

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the relevance of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in the life of a Muslim. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the relevance of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in the life of a Muslim.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Ulum al- Hadith in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the relevance of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in the life of a Muslim. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Practise the teachings of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in daily life

What this means
In this part you learn to practise the teachings of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in daily life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise the teachings of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in daily life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise the teachings of the Hadith on accountability and respect for authority in daily life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Ulum al- Hadith is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Ulum al- Hadith” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Ulum al- Hadith in your own words. (skill: explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: apply the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith)

Example 4: Show how “Ulum al- Hadith” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: value Hadith as a primary source of guidance)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Ulum al- Hadith to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs.
3. Practise this skill: explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith.
4. Practise this skill: apply the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Ulum al- Hadith from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Ulum al- Hadith: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Ulum al- Hadith?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What role did the Prophet (S.A.W.) play in the development of Hadith?
2. Why is it important for a Muslim to learn Ulum al- Hadith?
3. Why is intention important in Islam?
4. Why should Muslims respect authority?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Ulum al- Hadith means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the factors that led to the development of Hadith during the time of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and the Rightly Guided Caliphs.
5. Be able to: explain the methods used by the Prophet (S.A.W.) to teach Hadith.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
